help.title: How to play
help.p1: In interactive fiction, you read a story and decide what the hero does next. The game describes where you are; you answer with a short command.
help.p2: Commands are simple sentences: a verb, often an object. LOOK, TAKE LAMP, OPEN THE DOOR, READ LETTER, TALK TO THE GUARD.
help.p3: To move, use the compass: NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST, UP, DOWN, or just N, S, E, W, U, D. INVENTORY (I) lists what you carry.
help.p4: No need to type everything: the buttons under the text offer common verbs and the objects of the scene. Tap one, then another, to build a command.
help.p5: Stuck? EXAMINE everything, try HINT or HELP in the game, and read the room description again: the answer is often there.
help.p6: Your progress is saved after every turn on this device. The reader menu also has Undo and five save slots.
help.p7: Turn pages by tapping the edges of the screen or with the ‹ › buttons. The "Start here" badge marks games that are kind to beginners.

about.intro: Inkventure lets you play interactive fiction from IFDB on an e-reader. It is free, open-source software under the MIT licence.
about.ifdb: Catalogue data from IFDB, the Interactive Fiction Database (ifdb.org). Cover art is shown from IFDB. Each game belongs to its authors: see its IFDB page for its terms.
about.archive: Game files are downloaded from the IF Archive (ifarchive.org), hosted by the Interactive Fiction Technology Foundation.
about.engines: Z-machine games run on ZVM (ifvms.js, MIT licence) with GlkOte (glkote-term, MIT licence); Glulx games on Quixe (MIT licence), by Andrew Plotkin; ink stories on inkjs (MIT licence); Twine stories on their own story format, in a sandboxed frame. Built with Preact (MIT licence) and fflate (MIT licence).
about.fonts: Fonts: Literata and Source Sans 3, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
about.privacy: Privacy: there is no account, no tracking and no advertising. Your settings, progress and saved games stay in this browser. The app only downloads the catalogue from its own site, covers from IFDB and game files from the IF Archive.
about.ebook: Free ebook: a short guide to interactive fiction with games to start from its pages, in English and French. Download it from a computer at {address}
about.source: Source code: github.com/yciabaud/inkventure. The licences of the software and fonts it uses, in full: {address}
ebookPage.title: The Inkventure ebook
ebookPage.intro: A free guide to interactive fiction on e-readers, with a selection of games you can start from its pages. Download it on this computer, then copy it to your e-reader.
ebookPage.description: What interactive fiction is, how to play, how Inkventure works on your e-reader, and game cards with a “Play now” link.
ebookPage.hint.azw3: for e-readers that use the AZW3 (KF8) format
ebookPage.unavailable: The ebooks are not available here right now. They are built with each update of the main site (previews of changes do not have them): try again later.
ebookPage.howUsb: With a USB cable: connect the e-reader to the computer, open it like a USB drive, copy the file into its documents or books folder, then eject it.
ebookPage.howWireless: Without a cable: many e-readers have their own service to send a document by email or from a web page. Send the file there; your e-reader's help explains how.
ebookPage.howOpen: Then open the book from the e-reader's library. Its “Play now” links open the e-reader's web browser, sometimes after asking you to confirm.
ebookPage.noScript: This page needs JavaScript to list the books.
